{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantifies the concordance between mouse models and human clinical outcomes for chronic liver disease by analyzing gene expression patterns and calculating recall and precision metrics. It directly compares animal model results to human data, fulfilling the inclusion criteria.",
  "arm": "methods-and-bias",
  "arm_evidence": "The study revisits gene-expression changes in mouse models of liver damage and compares them with the human situation, aiming to address the question of whether experiments with mice allow meaningful conclusions to be drawn about the pathophysiology of CLDs in humans.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on chronic liver diseases (CLDs) and analyzes transcriptomic data from mouse models of liver damage and human liver tissue.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes data from seven mouse models (one chronic, six acute) and compares them with five human CLD cohorts, integrating various models to assess cross-species consistency.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly analyzes transcriptome data from 227 mice and compares it with human CLD expression data.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study analyzes RNA-sequencing data and gene expression changes, which are considered secondary biomarkers in this context."
}
